criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.
Given the data files, when any tab renders, then its content comes from .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json read at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given .colaberry/manifest.json, when any tab is shown, then it displays how old the data is and warns when that age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given the fields listing page, when a customer opens it, then all soccer fields with their current availability are shown.
Given a field with no open slots, when a customer views it, then it is clearly marked unavailable.
Given an available field, when a customer selects a date and time and confirms, then the booking is created and confirmed to the customer.
Given a field already booked for the selected slot, when a customer attempts to book it, then the booking is rejected with a clear reason.
Given a customer question about pricing or availability, when it is asked to the AI assistant, then an accurate answer is returned.
Given a refund or complaint request, when it is submitted, then it is routed to a human for approval before any action is taken.
Given a pending refund/complaint decision, when a human approves or denies it, then the outcome is recorded and the customer is notified.
Given two booking requests for overlapping times on the same field, when the second is submitted, then the system flags a conflict before it is confirmed.
Given a booking request, when the AI scheduling assistant processes it, then it proposes a slot that avoids known conflicts.
Given booking data over a period, when the analytics agent runs, then it produces a summary of trends including busy and slow periods.
Given a complex customer query beyond pricing/availability, when it is asked, then the AI provides a relevant answer or escalates it appropriately.
Given a customer service issue that cannot be resolved by AI alone, when it is identified, then it is escalated to a human.
Given expected user load, when the system is under typical usage, then interactions remain within an acceptable response time.
Given any booking action, when it occurs, then an audit trail entry is recorded with who, what and when.
Given a system auditor reviewing the audit trail, when they trace a booking, then they can follow it back to its origin.
Given a scheduling issue such as a conflict or cancellation, when it is detected, then the affected users are notified.
